title: Learned representations
goals: Trace an input through a hidden representation and a decision rule
Identify distinctions that a representation preserves or loses
Separate a useful constructed feature from evidence of successful learning
vocabulary: An encoding of an example used by another computation
A value produced inside a network after applying an activation function
Two different inputs receiving the same representation
A feature whose computation depends on parameters adjusted using training data

worked_example.title: See a collision and its consequences

blocks.title: Different rectangles can share a hidden vector
blocks.caption: The representation preserves the wider-than-height answer for these examples but discards information needed to recover their different areas. A deterministic head receiving only this vector must give both examples the same output.

blocks.label: Encode [6, 4] and [7, 5]. Give their wider-than-height predictions and areas. Can a head that sees only h always recover the exact area? Explain using this pair.

guided_practice.title: Prove an information loss
guided_practice.prompt: Give the hidden vectors and areas for [4, 2] and [5, 3]. Explain why increasing only the complexity of a deterministic area head cannot make both exact predictions correct.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Both hidden vectors are [2, 0], while areas are 8 and 15 square cm. Identical inputs to a deterministic head yield identical outputs, so the head cannot return both required values.

independent_case.title: Audit a new representation independently
independent_case.task: A different layer uses g = [ReLU(width - height - 1), ReLU(height - width - 1)]. Encode [4, 3] and [3, 4]. State their targets for width strictly greater than height. Can any deterministic head receiving only g classify both correctly?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Both encode as [0, 0]: the scores are [0, -2] and [-2, 0]. Targets are 1 and 0. No deterministic head receiving only this shared vector can distinguish the pair. The added threshold erased a distinction required by this task.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: Two hidden values preserve both input measurements
Dimension alone does not guarantee recovery; distinct inputs can collide.
A more complex head can always fix lost information
A deterministic head cannot distinguish identical representations without additional input.
Correct outputs prove human concepts were learned
The layer here was constructed, and a task score alone does not establish a hidden concept.

blocks.text: A prediction head is the computation that reads the hidden vector and produces an output. Keeping it separate lets us inspect what information is available before making a decision. This example assumes two finite, positive measurements in cm; it is not a general input validator.

blocks.title: Optional Python check

blocks.text: The raw difference width - height can be recovered as h1 - h2. The original width and height cannot in general be recovered: many rectangles share a difference. Two hidden components do not guarantee preservation of two input components.
